body:
`.github/workflows/tests.yml` resolves the container under test to `ghcr.io/new-usemame/calibre-web-nextgen:dev` for anything that is not a version tag (lines 537-542), and the step that injects the code under test — "Overlay this PR's SPA bundle into the container" (line 776) — is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (line 777).

On a **push to main** the overlay is therefore skipped and nothing from the head commit reaches the container. The suite runs against the `:dev` image published by the PREVIOUS merge.

It is not a race that sometimes loses; it loses every time. Observed on merge commit `2bae9887b`:

    21:32:14  E2E Tests (SPA) job starts
    21:32:22  "Testing image: ghcr.io/new-usemame/calibre-web-nextgen:dev"   <- pull happens here
    21:32:28  build-amd64 for this commit starts
    21:34:22  build-amd64 completes — the :dev containing this commit first exists 2 min AFTER the pull

The e2e leg pulls `:dev` roughly 8 seconds into the run; the `:dev` carrying the head commit does not publish for about another two minutes.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A WASTED JOB. `auto-revert` reads this leg and acts on the premise *"Test Suite failed on a main push therefore the head commit broke it."* Because the leg tests the previous build, a failure is attributed to a commit whose code was never in the container. #1563 reverted a docs-only commit on exactly this basis. #1564 filters e2e-only failures, which stops the immediate bleeding but leaves the attribution broken for any other consumer of the same signal.

It also mis-frames the four failures that surfaced when #1557 first made e2e run on a main push. They are not "breakage that was always there and finally became visible" — they are failures of whichever `:dev` was live at that moment, i.e. of code that merged one step earlier.

And it degrades the standard flake control. Re-running a PR on an unchanged head does NOT hold the artifact constant, because `:dev` can move between the two runs. A negative result from that control is weaker than it looks.

FIX OPTIONS, in preference order:
1. On a main push, wait for this commit's image build and pull it **by digest**, so the artifact under test is pinned to the commit being judged.
2. Or run the overlay on `push` as well as `pull_request` (it already builds the SPA from the checkout).
3. Failing both, make `auto-revert` refuse to act on any leg that cannot name the digest it tested.

NOTE FOR VERIFICATION GENERALLY: a step count proves the suite RAN; it cannot prove it ran against the code you think it did. Both guards are needed and they are independent.
title: The main-push e2e leg tests :dev, not the commit being pushed
